title: SUMPRODUCT: multiply the pair, then add them up

docs.syntax: =SUMPRODUCT(prices, quantities) multiplies the two ranges row by row and adds the products
docs.explain:
SUMPRODUCT pairs two ranges row by row, multiplies each pair, then adds the products. The formula =SUMPRODUCT(B2:B4,C2:C4) covers the three prices and the three quantities and returns 100. Ten times two, five times four and twenty times three come to 20, 20 and 60. A helper column of products would reach the same answer, in more steps and in a second place to be wrong.

The second screen puts that pair of ranges in the numerator of an average. Divide 100 by the quantity total of 9 and the answer is 11.1, the average price per item, with the ink row counted three times. Averaging the three prices instead comes to 11.7, because each row counts once whatever its quantity.

Keep both ranges on the same rows. SUMPRODUCT pairs by position, so a range that starts one row late pairs each price with the wrong quantity and the total still reads as a number. Excel only objects with #VALUE! when the heights differ outright.

errors.text: The two ranges are a different height, so the pairs stop lining up and Excel refuses the call.
The function name is misspelt, so Excel reads it as an undefined name.
A range that starts one row below the other pairs each price with the next quantity, and the total comes back as a number.

docs.atWork: Valuing a stock list in one cell, and averaging a price per unit sold rather than per row.
docs.outcome: Value a table and take a weighted average from the same two columns.
docs.teaches: SUMPRODUCT as a value total and as the numerator of a weighted average
docs.dataset: Stock list with a price chain and a quantity per row

screens.prompt: In D5, total the value of the stock: price times quantity on every row, added up.

hints.syntax: =SUMPRODUCT(B2:B4,C2:C4): two ranges, one comma, no multiplication sign.
hints.func-sumproduct: Both columns go in, and the function does the multiplying and adding itself.
hints.require-ref: Point at the price and quantity cells, not at numbers typed into the formula.
hints.value: Ten times two, five times four, twenty times three: 100.
hints.error: The formula still divides something by zero, so the cell shows #DIV/0! in place of a stock value.

reject.why: one column adds the prices and ignores the quantities
one range on its own has nothing to pair with
the prices are multiplied by themselves, so the quantities never count
the first item is left out of both ranges
the total is divided by zero
the ranges sit outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D5, work out the average price paid per item, counting each row once per unit it holds.

hints.syntax: =ROUND(SUMPRODUCT(B2:B4,C2:C4)/SUM(C2:C4),1): the division sits inside the ROUND.
hints.func-sumproduct: The numerator is the value of the whole stock, so it is a pair of ranges.
hints.require-ref: Both totals, the value and the quantity, come from the table rows.
hints.value: 100 divided by 9 units is 11.111..., which rounds to 11.1.
hints.error: A zero denominator returns #DIV/0! before ROUND runs at all.

reject.why: the three rows are counted once each, not once per unit
the answer is left at eleven and a sixth, with no rounding
the price total is the wrong denominator
the first item is missing from the numerator
the answer is rounded to a whole number
the average is then divided by zero
the division falls outside the parentheses ROUND needs

seo.title: SUMPRODUCT in Excel: price times quantity
seo.description: SUMPRODUCT pairs two ranges row by row, multiplies, then adds, so a stock list is valued in one cell. Divide by the total quantity for a weighted average.
